answer: Give every agent identity a slow-growth trust root: new agents enter through a narrow inlet with capped rewards and must perform verifiable useful work continuously over a long horizon before earning full economic rights. Trust compounds like a cedar — deep roots built from months of consistent behavior, not a one-time payment. A sybil operator would have to sustain real work across every fake identity for months, turning a cheap identity flood into an expensive, slow farm that costs more than it earns.
